# Merchant receivables and service billing

Follow the [complete merchant financial workflow](../merchant-workspace/FINANCIAL_OPERATIONS.md) for original Stellar reconciliation, customer billing, dated payment plans, Xero handover and full operating recovery in this same accounting workspace.

Operate a merchant's complete invoice and customer-payment cycle in the original private accounting workspace. The product brings customer records, service quotations, issued invoices, payment allocation, credit notes and dated account delivery into one installed operator.

The maintained `merchant-receivables` selection includes the invoice and quotation workflow, typed HTTP and MCP clients, Stellar wallet collection, customer payment plans, dated collections, accounting and support commands, their explicit package exports and managed Applications adapters. It uses the existing accounting writer and customer UUIDs, the SF74 quotation engine and the source distribution's installation, lifecycle and recovery. `starforge registrations` shows the inventory in the installed source edition.

## Install the selected product

Use the current maintained repository and an exact commit that contains [the receivables selection](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/selections/merchant-receivables.json). The source builder packages that commit through the existing Git reader, original browser manifests and dependency collector.

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/merchant-checkout --ref FULL_COMMIT_SHA \
  --selection merchant-receivables --out /private/receivables-release
~~~

Use the archive path and SHA256 returned by that command. The retained output belongs to that source commit and selection. To continue the same output after interruption:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/merchant-checkout \
  --out /private/receivables-release --resume

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --out /private/receivables-release --status
~~~

The original Runtime workspace also discovers this recipe in **Build a product**. Select **Merchant receivables and Stellar invoice collection**, review its exact source, then open the completed archive in **Source & profile**. The package version includes both the source commit and `selection.merchant-receivables`.

The complete installed accounting, quotation and managed-operator profile uses the existing Linux runtime: Node 22.16+, Python 3.11+, npm, `flock` and the original archive utilities. Prepare the selected original dependencies through the maintained installer:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs prepare \
  --dir /private/receivables-runtime \
  --archive /absolute/returned-package.tgz --sha256 RETURNED_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --native --feature schema --feature openapi --feature mcp --operator

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs install \
  --dir /private/receivables-runtime

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs inspect \
  --dir /private/receivables-runtime --load --source
~~~

The native feature equips the existing Stellar verification/recovery paths; schema and OpenAPI belong to the original source and quotation-support workflows. The MCP feature equips the original merchant agent host and its HTTP and stdio interfaces. The installer selects their actual declared versions. An already retained matching dependency graph can be received with its original lock and the installer's `--adopt-existing` option. Use `resume --dir /private/receivables-runtime` to continue that same prepared installation.

The installed package stays in `/private/receivables-runtime/package/`, beside the selected `node_modules/`. Run its original command through that layout:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs run \
  --dir /private/receivables-runtime -- receivables help
~~~

The remaining examples use the installed `starforge` command. The same arguments can be passed after `runtime-install ... run --`.

## Connect the original accounting workspace

An initialized accounting workspace is reopened using its existing directory:

~~~sh
starforge receivables serve \
  --directory /private/merchant/accounting --port 8448
~~~

For first initialization, select the merchant's actual source outbox, proof directory and accounting terms. Keep the accounting directory outside those input directories:

~~~sh
starforge receivables serve \
  --directory /private/merchant/accounting \
  --outbox /private/merchant/source/outbox \
  --proof-dir /private/merchant/source/proofs \
  --terms /private/merchant/source/terms.json \
  --port 8448
~~~

The original initializer validates the selected private paths and terms before saving. Existing records keep their actual customer, order, report and source identities.

Open the printed local URL. **Customers and statements** opens the original customer manager in that same process. Add or update the customer's billing address, reference and contact details there. Back in receivables, save the issuer name, document prefixes and payment instructions in Settings. The same customer UUID is used for quotations, invoices, receipts and account exports.

In the existing Runtime workspace, attach this installed runtime and use **Applications**:

~~~sh
starforge runtime-workspace init --workspace /private/receivables-operator

starforge runtime-workspace attach \
  --workspace /private/receivables-operator \
  --runtime /private/receivables-runtime --label "Merchant billing"

starforge runtime-workspace serve \
  --workspace /private/receivables-operator --port 8465
~~~

Choose **Merchant receivables**, select the initialized accounting directory, and use Review, Save, Start and Open. The source-owned adapter binds the original workspace ID and source configuration and rechecks them inside the accounting lease. **Merchant accounting** opens the maintained reconciliation/connection workflow; **Merchant support** opens the existing cases and quotation workflow.

One process owns an accounting directory at a time. Use the running process's customer, receivables and **Payment plans** views together. **Customer payment plans** in Applications opens the same combined server directly at its collection desk. Stop that process through its original application before opening the directory with another owner.

## Close customer statements from the merchant connection

**Customer statements** in Applications opens the complete customer closing workbench included in this merchant receivables package. Select the original running merchant MCP address, its accounting workspace alias, the named operator and a private folder for saved customer closing work. The access token stays in the original environment or a private environment file.

Review, save, start and open that application through the existing Runtime workspace. The original startup records the local opening address with the reviewed merchant connection and saved-work folder. Reopen the same folder after a restart or package upgrade.

~~~sh
starforge customer-closing \
  --directory /private/merchant/customer-closes \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp \
  --workspace accounting --actor operator --port 4419
~~~

Use **Customers and service** to create or edit billing profiles, assign original order references, compare them with a retained accounting run and import configured service captures. Every change is reviewed and saved before application. The same saved request can be reconciled or resumed after an interrupted reply.

Choose customers, accounting runs and the original opening and closing service captures in **Compose a cycle**. Review each customer's complete native statement before issuing the selected closing cycle. Progress, original statement identities and completed files stay available during a resumed close. **Download customer delivery** provides that customer's full original files; the whole-cycle download preserves the complete operator folder for continued work.

Issued statements expose the original customer details, complete history and retained files. Prepare a correction from that original statement to retain its customer, sources and period; withdrawals record an explicit reason while preserving its original files and history. Customer profile edits update the source customer while issued documents keep their original billing details.

The [complete customer closing guide](../../stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/ACCOUNTING_STATEMENT_WORKBENCH.md) covers customer intake, capture configuration, closing cycles, correction, withdrawal, saved-operation recovery, file delivery and the typed interfaces. The workbench uses the original accounting writer through the existing MCP host.

## From service quotation to invoice

The original Merchant support desk creates and retains commercial quotations. Its existing commercial guide and command remain packaged:

~~~sh
starforge merchant-commercial --help
~~~

Prepare the quotation from the selected implementation, service and original pricing sources. Review its original calculation and publish the selected edition. Download the complete retained QUOTE material or QUOTE_JSON. The source case retains the separate RESPONSE material for a chosen customer response.

In receivables, choose those original files, select the existing accounting customer, dates and currency precision, then choose a billing scope:

| Scope | Selected charge |
| --- | --- |
| IMPLEMENTATION | The quotation's one-time implementation lines, charged once. |
| RECURRING | Service and planned route-usage lines multiplied by an explicit positive number of monthly periods and a specific period label. |

For recurring charges, use an explicit label such as `October–December 2026` and a count of three. Enter the intended issue and due dates separately.

The compiler checks the original canonical quote seal, draft and calculation review; complete source line totals; and a supplied response's binding to that exact quote edition. It preserves both original case IDs when a receiving case records the response. The accounting customer mapping is explicit.

The resulting invoice is an editable draft. Review the scope, currency precision, purchase order, tax, dates and individual charges before issue. The full mapping retains original line identifiers, quantities, rates, micro-USD extended amounts, selected periods and each rounding difference. Planned usage keeps its original description. The chosen matching ACCEPTED response appears in the retained quote review.

An implementation charge cannot be duplicated by changing a period label. Recurring imports retain their exact quote, customer, scope, period count and label. The complete original quote, chosen response, calculation source and review are downloadable from the invoice's source record. Later manual edits to the imported draft remain visible.

The original SF74 operating documents are included at:

- [Commercial quotation workflow](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/COMMERCIAL.md).
- [Full commercial receiving](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/commercial/RECEIVING.md).
- [Receivables source/operator guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/receivables/README.md).

### Quotes with a selected tariff

The same import accepts the original tariff-bearing quotation and its response. **Tariff at quote import** shows the saved selection volume, quoted monthly volume, accepted uniform rate, original tariff total and unit-rounding difference. The service-agreement desk presents the same basis beside each accepted quote edition and its billing preview.

The quoted route amount remains the amount to bill. The original tariff comparison may show a different total when a revised quotation changes its monthly request volume. For example, the [original tariff receiving journey](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/commercial/tariff-receiving-native.mjs) selects 1,250 requests, then publishes a revision for 1,500 requests. That revision retains the saved USD 0.0114 uniform rate and quotes USD 17.10 per month; its separately retained tier comparison at 1,500 requests totals USD 16.50. Selecting two recurring periods therefore imports USD 34.20 at two-place invoice precision.

The importer checks the tariff binding against the quote's selected pricing source, its original file-descriptor identity, scenario plan, selected route, quoted volume and uniform rate. It preserves the source pricing version and the tariff operation's completed pricing version as their separate original identities. The quote's original canonical seal, draft seal, review seal, calculated line totals and matching response are checked by the existing importer.

The complete selected tariff binding is retained in `source.json`, including original material identity and byte hash, both tariff file descriptors, native selection UUID, plan and comparison identities, tier schedule, and the saved-versus-quoted calculation basis. Its associated pricing source retains its original material and five file descriptors. Each selected route line also carries its tariff source and comparison identities. `review.json` identifies the included invoice line, whole period count, original monthly amount and imported charge.

The original `quote.json` and `response.json` bytes remain downloadable beside that source and review. An implementation-only import retains the tariff as quotation context; its selected invoice lines remain the one-time implementation charges. Recurring import includes the original service and planned-route lines for the chosen monthly periods. Later invoice edits retain the import's original source and its visible changed-draft indicator.

Accepted tariff quotations can also supply the [service-agreement calendar](../merchant-service-agreements/README.md). Each period uses that same importer, and the agreement's source JSON, calculation review and complete source downloads carry the tariff through billing and later export.

### Accepted revisions informed by recorded usage

A revised Commercial quote may also carry its original `sourceBindings.performance`. The same import retains this complete binding and joins its explicit proposed monthly volume, target tariff/pricing source, accepted unit rate and original extended amount to the revised quote's route. The measured quote and selected historical tariff keep their own identities; a revision may intentionally choose a different saved tariff.

Both billing operators display the earlier quote, observed period and quantity basis, saved price and tier comparison at that quantity, then the revised monthly volume and accepted charge. The saved native cost view, individual source counts, usage version/revision and full source identities remain available with that review. Billing uses the accepted revised monthly amount for the selected whole periods.

`source.json` retains the native performance source ID, saved review ID/hash, original material and source-file descriptors, measured quote/tariff/selection, observed period/basis, recorded quote/tariff/cost view, original issues and complete proposed pricing fields. `review.json` keeps that same binding and identifies its included invoice line and selected amount. The raw quotation and matching customer response continue through the ordinary source downloads and agreement export. The complete underlying usage export remains in the original Commercial case and its recipient package, addressed by the retained file and material identities.

## Issue and deliver the invoice

Create a manual invoice or continue an imported quotation draft. Monetary fields are decimal strings at an explicit currency precision. Quantities support six decimal places. Line discounts, invoice discounts and tax amounts are explicit.

Save the draft, review its current preview, then issue it. The current customer and issuer details participate in that review. Issuing assigns the configured prefix, issue year and next workspace sequence and creates immutable invoice JSON, a line CSV, printable HTML and its file manifest.

Download the original issued files for the customer's usual delivery channel. The printable invoice displays line and invoice discounts, taxes, dates, payment instructions and the frozen billing identity. Later changes to a customer address or issuer settings leave that issued document's original content intact.

## Receive money and allocate it

Record a payment with the accounting customer, currency and precision, received date, method, reference and amount. The ledger distinguishes the payment's total amount from amounts allocated to invoices. A partial allocation leaves the balance available for that customer's later invoices.

Choose the invoice, amount and effective allocation date. The controller requires matching customer and currency and checks both the selected date and all affected later intervals. A backdated allocation therefore preserves money already used by a later allocation.

A native Stellar settlement can be imported from a completed original accounting report. Select the original ledger event and customer order binding, then enter the commercial-currency valuation and basis. The receipt retains the native report, event, transaction fingerprint, asset and atomic amount. Its existing public-network transfer and official RPC verification remain the payment evidence.

Correct an allocation with a dated release and reason. Its original history remains visible and the receipt becomes available from that date. A receipt or invoice can be voided once applicable allocations have been released. A credited invoice retains its issued credit-note history.

## Return customer funds or move paid credit

Open **Receipts** and choose **Refund / credit**, or use **Manage customer funds** on a paid invoice with an issued credit. The desk lists the customer's original receipts, available funds, paid credits, reserved refunds and completed refunds for the selected accounting date.

Choose the original receipt. An unapplied overpayment can fund a refund directly. For a paid invoice credit, enter the exact credited amount to release from its payment allocation. Review shows the remaining payment against that invoice and the resulting receipt balance. The original allocation is retained with its dated release and the exact remaining payment is recorded as a replacement. Every affected later date is checked before saving.

For a refund, choose the actual payment route:

| Route | Operator workflow |
| --- | --- |
| Completed refund | Record the completed payment's actual method, reference and date, then review and save the customer cash movement. |
| Stellar wallet | Review the merchant paying account, customer destination, network, asset, exact transfer amount and commercial valuation. The public-network request reserves the reviewed customer funds. Open the retained wallet request, record its returned hash and receive the original transaction. |
| Original verified payout | Select an original verified return that still needs its customer accounting entry. Review derives its ledger date, sender, destination, asset, memo and native proof from that retained transfer. |
| Original verified adjustment | Select the receipt's unused original verified Stellar refund adjustment and review its commercial value and exact source binding. |

The review displays the receipt's allocated, reserved, refunded and available amounts before and after the change, together with every affected invoice's paid, due and credited amounts. Save that complete review to retain the refund and its original customer documents. Test-network requests and observations are identified in the desk.

**Move credit** uses the same original receipt and credited allocations. Select the actual outstanding invoices in that customer's currency, enter the amounts to apply and review the complete result. A remaining amount stays available in the customer account.

A pending wallet refund can be cancelled with an effective date and reason. The original request and allocation history remain visible. If a payment arrives after cancellation, or a second actual transfer is discovered, retain its hash and receive it against that original request. The customer-funds desk offers the verified unposted payout for a new review when its accounting needs correction. For an operator-recorded refund entered in error, reverse the original and use **Correct recorded refund** to prepare its linked replacement. Keep the actual bank payment date and date the cash correction on the original reversal; both dates and the original documents remain visible.

The customer account export includes original refund and disposition records, customer documents alongside invoices, credit notes, receipts and allocation history. Open **Saved refund files** for the complete original transaction receiving record and individual native proofs. The [refund and credit operating guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/receivables/REFUNDS_AND_CREDITS.md) covers browser, HTTP, CLI and merchant-agent operation with durable request recovery.

## Credit a customer and close a period

Issue a credit against original invoice lines with explicit net and tax amounts. Cumulative credits cannot exceed those original line amounts. A credit after full payment appears as a customer credit balance.

Choose the as-of date before reviewing balances, invoice details and aging. Amounts remain separate for every currency and precision. The aging table distinguishes current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90 and 91+ day balances.

Download the complete customer account TAR, including its issued invoice and credit-note files and manifest. JSON, CSV and printable account views are available independently. Customer exports select issued documents effective on the chosen date and the corresponding receipt references and allocation history.

Useful original commands:

~~~sh
starforge receivables state \
  --directory /private/merchant/accounting --as-of 2026-10-31

starforge receivables detail \
  --directory /private/merchant/accounting --id INVOICE_UUID \
  --as-of 2026-10-31

starforge receivables export \
  --directory /private/merchant/accounting --customer CUSTOMER_UUID \
  --as-of 2026-10-31 --out /private/new-october-account
~~~

Exports use a new output directory. The existing customer statements, accounting pricing, native reconciliation and recovery commands remain available in the same installed selection.

## Schedule and collect an invoice balance

Open **Payment plans** from the running receivables navigation. Choose an issued invoice and balance date, enter its installment dates and amounts or generate equal installments, save the draft, review the complete invoice basis and activate the customer schedule. Every edition retains printable HTML, CSV, JSON and its file manifest.

The desk applies the same recorded allocations, releases and credit notes to the dated schedule. It separates overdue, due-today, upcoming, after-horizon and unscheduled amounts by currency and decimal precision. Revised editions preserve earlier schedule files and historical views; a dated cancellation returns the remaining invoice amount to unscheduled collections.

The [complete payment-plan operating guide](../merchant-payment-plans/README.md) covers schedule preparation, collections, customer files, recovery and the installed HTTP/CLI interfaces. This receivables selection includes that same implementation, command, browser assets and managed **Customer payment plans** application. The `merchant-payment-plans` selection packages the same accounting and quotation dependencies with the payment-plan guide as its product entry.

## Continue after interruption or upgrade

Each receivables mutation retains the named operator, current accounting revision and original request ID. Draft updates also retain their expected version; issue retains the reviewed preview hash.

When a request's outcome is uncertain, retain that exact pending request. The operator disables another mutation until the original outcome is resolved. If the accounting writer requests reopening, stop and reopen the same original directory, then retry the same request ID and content. The saved accounting journal determines whether it already completed.

An edited draft remains parked when changing selection or importing a quotation, and can be resumed. A stale accounting revision requires reviewing the current saved state before applying a subsequent change.

All receivables state is under the original `workspace.json.receivables`; customer identities remain under `workspace.json.customerStatements`. Issued documents and source-quotation files use the existing private `exports/` tree. The maintained accounting backup captures those files with the workspace.

For an upgrade, prepare a new runtime for the selected new source archive, retain the old runtime and original accounting directory, then use the maintained runtime compare/recovery workflow. Stop the prior owner, review the same accounting binding in the new application, and reopen the existing issued documents and dated account.

## Programmatic interfaces

| Package export | Original interface |
| --- | --- |
| `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/receivables` | ReceivablesWorkspace over an open AccountingWorkspace. |
| `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/receivables/core` | Exact invoice/credit compilation, balances, aging and customer rendering. |
| `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/receivables/quote-import` | Pure original quotation/response-to-draft compilation. |
| `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/receivables/client` | Typed HTTP client for the same operation and file contracts. |
| `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/receivables/server` | Complete loopback server or handler over the existing open workspace. |
| `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/accounting-receivables` | Typed client for invoices, collection, customer files and request recovery through the existing accounting MCP owner. |
| `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/accounting-receivables/operations` | Durable operation preparation, execution, reconciliation and original file downloads. |

Use the actual package name shown by the installed `package.json` and retain the suffixes above. The original distribution exports are explicit; `starforge registrations --source merchant-receivables` prints this product's command, client, browser and Applications registrations.

## Collect an invoice through a Stellar wallet

Open an issued invoice and use **Stellar payment requests** to prepare collection terms. The review binds the request to the original customer, invoice document and current amount due. Choose the public network or test network, the merchant's exact receiving account, the asset and amount in Stellar units, and the amount of the commercial invoice that the transfer will settle. When the asset value differs from the invoice currency, retain the agreed valuation in the request.

Issue the reviewed request, then share its wallet link or original `payment-request.html` document. Each request has its own invoice-bound memo. The operator can issue separate partial collection requests, inspect saved returns, cancel replaced instructions and download the original request and full receiving record.

After the customer sends the payment, record the transaction hash returned by their wallet and use **Receive**. The native verifier uses the original Stellar RPC catalogue and official SDK to check the ledger transaction's network, destination, payer constraint when selected, asset issuer, exact amount, memo and successful operation result. It supports classic payments, strict-send and strict-receive path payments, and fee-bump transactions reported by either their inner or outer hash.

A verified public-network transfer produces an original customer receipt and dated invoice allocation. Both fee-bump hash identities participate in duplicate detection. Full native proof is retained as original private files and hydrated for downloads; the accounting journal keeps a compact reference. Test-network receiving remains visible as a verified test observation. All original invoice documents retain their issued content as payments and balances change.

The [complete payment request guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/receivables/PAYMENT_REQUESTS.md) covers browser operation, CLI requests, the typed HTTP client, exact file names and recovery of interrupted work.

## Operate receivables through the merchant agent interface

The original merchant MCP host now exposes the same invoice and collection workflow through 35 `merchant_accounting_receivables_*` operations. A configured accounting workspace supplies the original customers, journal, private exports and source aliases. The agent can import a service quotation, prepare and issue an invoice, create reviewed Stellar wallet instructions, receive a returned transaction, refund customer funds, move paid credit, apply receipts and deliver the dated customer account in that one owner.

The installed client command uses the host's configured endpoint, workspace alias and access-token environment variable:

~~~sh
starforge merchant-accounting-receivables sources \
  --url "$MERCHANT_MCP_URL" --workspace "$MERCHANT_WORKSPACE" \
  --token-env MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN

starforge merchant-accounting-receivables status \
  --url "$MERCHANT_MCP_URL" --workspace "$MERCHANT_WORKSPACE" \
  --token-env MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN
~~~

Use complete native previews for invoice issue and payment-request creation. The client retains the full original document or wallet proposal and its review SHA. Durable `prepare`, `execute` and `reconcile` commands keep the original arguments, request ID, source revision and connection in a private operation directory. An interrupted reply is reconciled against the existing accounting journal; configured quotation aliases reconcile to the exact source bytes archived by the original import.

Native invoice and credit files, quotation sources, preview files, wallet instructions, refund records, transaction proofs and the complete customer account are available through the existing retained file reader. Downloads retain their original selectors, read ID and SHA through every chunk. Ordinary client commands drain their own retained reads; `close` explicitly finishes the accounting owner.

The [complete agent interface guide](../../stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/ACCOUNTING_RECEIVABLES.md) includes configured source aliases, customer and issuer intake, an invoice-to-payment workflow, all 35 tools, typed client examples, file selectors and durable operation recovery. Use the original [merchant accounting host guide](../../stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/ACCOUNTING.md) to configure and start that owner.

## Original native exercise

The product includes one complete private-file exercise:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/receivables/EXERCISE.mjs
~~~

It uses the actual accounting workspace and original SF74 commissioning, quote review, seal and document producer. It creates its own private temporary accounting directory and completes invoice issue, payments and dated allocations, credit, historical release/backdating checks, one-time and recurring quote imports, exact source downloads, customer export, close/reopen and actual HTTP requests.

The same programme is retained under `SCF-MERCHANT-RECEIVABLES-DFF77-20261012`. Its complete 65-member source capsule, including the original license, is Git blob `87452bd68e4208e6d48ed18bcdea24dcf3da1152` in `woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026`. The capsule contains the full UTF-8 body and original Git identity for every member. Its selected exercised path uses Node builtins.

[Source lineage](SOURCE_LINEAGE.json) retains the exact adopted public product, original accounting dependency files and existing quotation/customer source identities. The original accounting, SF74, native transfer and distribution owners continue to maintain those components.

# Merchant Support

This package contains the original Merchant Support product selected from the source commit and `merchant-support` recipe recorded in `manifest.json`.

Operate the same saved merchant case through incidents, implementation, native source editions, Service commitments, native adjustments, buyer credit coding, period close, accountant handoff, recorded usage and customer pricing revisions, commercial quotations, accepted change orders and complete customer receiving. The browser, command line and installed Support agent use the original case and native delivery engines.

## Open the complete guides

- [Product overview](source/products/merchant-support/README.md)
- [Operating instructions and agent setup](source/products/merchant-support/OPERATING.md)
- [Runtime installation and complete customer receiving](source/products/merchant-support/RECEIVING.md)
- [Complete delivery browser and sixteen package tools](source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/CASE_PACKAGE_WORKSPACE.md)
- [Native case and source package](source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/CASE_SOURCE_PACKAGE.md)
- [Service adjustments and complete native delivery](source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/SERVICE_ADJUSTMENT_HANDOVER.md)
- [Buyer period and accountant receiving](source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/SERVICE_BUYER_HANDOVER.md)
- [Commercial pricing-workspace receiving](source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/commercial/RECEIVING.md)
- [Tariff quotation and complete customer receiving](source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/commercial/TARIFFS.md)
- [Supplier costs, original tariff planning and pricing adoption](source/products/merchant-economics/OPERATING.md)
- [Recorded usage, complete performance source and native pricing proposals](source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf97-merchant-revenue-ops/performance/README.md)
- [Performance-backed customer quote revisions](source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/commercial/PERFORMANCE.md)
- [Accepted quotations, implementation and change orders](source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf74-merchant-support-console/COMMERCIAL_IMPLEMENTATION.md)

Every linked guide is included as an original file under `source/`.

## Install the original runtime

Use this archive's actual SHA-256 with the maintained runtime profile and installer. Select the original `schema`, `openapi`, `mcp`, native and operator dependencies, then attach the READY runtime to Runtime workspace. Open **Applications → Merchant support** and select the customer's actual private case, source and package directories.

The optional accounting and buyer connection fields attach the existing native owners for Service adjustments, buyer periods and accountant work. The optional Handoffs profile connects the original remote receiving sources. The application retains its reviewed native profile identity through startup and reopening.

## Accepted quotations through delivery

1. Open **Commercial** for the actual saved merchant case. Prepare the quotation from its retained implementation, Service and pricing sources, then record the customer's response against the saved quote edition.
2. In **Implementation**, review the accepted edition's task and plan changes and its one-time and monthly amounts. Choose **Keep current edit** or **Use accepted scope** for overlapping edits, then select **Review selected choices**.
3. Enter **Recorded by** and an implementation note. Apply the reviewed scope to start the implementation or record an accepted change order. The same case retains the quotation, customer response, reviewed choices and previous commercial basis.
4. Choose **Open implementation and receiving** to assign the agreed tasks and attach their original deliverables. In **Technical and customer receiving**, use **Implementation plan tasks** for accepted custom work or select the original workorder edition for work tied to it. Record the actual technical or customer observation and its source reference.
5. In **Export and reopen**, choose **Open complete case handoff**. The original complete-delivery desk saves the case and retains the export and receiving operations for its full history, source bundles and attachments.

Later quotation revisions continue through the same review and acceptance workflow. The receiving case keeps the original agreement and accepted changes alongside the delivered work.

## Tariff quotation and editable handover

Open **Applications → Merchant pricing and scenario planning → Tariff planning** to retain the original schedule, compare exact quantities and complete its selected scenario and pricing requests. In **Applications → Merchant support → Commercial quotations**, choose the saved customer case and open **Tariff sources**.

Capture the completed original selection with its full pricing backup, inspect the retained source and attach it through the original case writer. The quote keeps its selected quantity, saved uniform rate, original tier total and rounding. A changed monthly quantity displays the original tariff calculation alongside the saved-rate charge.

Continue the accepted quotation into implementation and receiving. The complete case package carries the original tariff source and pricing backup with its quote editions, customer responses and delivery history. In the receiving case, restore the original pricing workspace, receive the selected portfolio and reopen both saved native outcomes.

The maintained commands are `starforge merchant-tariffs`, `starforge merchant-commercial tariffs` and the original `merchant-mcp pricing` and Support tools. The linked tariff guide provides the complete capture, three-request attachment, download, export and restoration inputs.

## Recorded usage through the next customer quotation

Use the original Pricing console's **Performance** page to compare a completed tariff selection with a saved usage source. The observed period, exact count basis, saved uniform quote and original tariff curve remain explicit. Save the review and export its complete original source.

In **Merchant support → Commercial quotations → Usage and revisions**, receive that full source against the measured original quote. Select the retained review, enter an explicit monthly request volume and choose the existing or a newer received native tariff for the same route. Prepare the ordinary quote draft, then complete its original review, publication, customer-response and accepted-work flow.

The full customer case carries the performance source as an original material. Its receiving case can inspect and export that source immediately. Complete native continuation uses an original Pricing workspace backup captured after the review and proposal operations, plus the full tariff portfolio. Restore that backup, receive the portfolio through its original owner and reopen Performance to recover the same saved proposal and selection requests.

The package includes `starforge merchant-performance`, `starforge merchant-commercial performance`, the typed `./merchant/performance-client` and `./merchant/commercial-performance-client` exports, and the original Pricing and Support MCP methods. Both linked performance guides describe the exact inputs, source identities, native request UUIDs, downloads and continuation.

## Accepted quotations through billing and the service calendar

Select the published quotation in the saved customer case and download its complete quotation JSON and matching accepted response. Open **Applications → Merchant receivables** or **Applications → Service agreements and billing** with the merchant's original initialized accounting directory and customer.

The invoice import retains the selected tariff and measured-usage source alongside the accepted revised amount. Its view separates the observed period and quantity from the explicitly quoted monthly volume and uniform rate. Review the source, billing scope, dates and resulting draft, then issue it through the original Receivables writer.

For ongoing work, create the service agreement from that same accepted source. Review its original monthly boundaries, billing periods and current quotation edition. Preparing a period creates the original invoice draft; later editions, renewals and cancellation preserve the previous calendar and bills. The same combined server exposes customer records, receivables and the service calendar under one accounting lease.

The package includes the original payment plans, Stellar collection, paid credits, refunds and customer statement closing. Its typed clients and merchant tools continue to use the original Accounting and service-agreement controllers.

- [Complete invoicing, payment and refund workflow](source/products/merchant-receivables/README.md)
- [Accepted agreements and recurring billing](source/products/merchant-service-agreements/README.md)
- [Payment plans and dated collections](source/products/merchant-payment-plans/README.md)
- [Complete financial operation](source/products/merchant-workspace/FINANCIAL_OPERATIONS.md)

## Commands

The installed `starforge` command includes `receivables`, `service-agreements`, `payment-plans`, `customer-closing`, `merchant-accounting-receivables`, `merchant-accounting-pricing`, `merchant-accounting-recovery`, `support-console`, `support-watch`, `merchant-implementation`, `merchant-services`, `merchant-commercial`, `merchant-tariffs`, `merchant-performance`, `merchant-support-agent`, `merchant-service-adjustments`, `merchant-service-adjustment-receiving`, `merchant-accounting-adjustments`, `buyer-expenses`, the original merchant MCP launchers, and the maintained runtime installation and transfer commands.

Read the setup command's original options:

```sh
starforge merchant-support-agent --help
```

The setup command creates the original merchant host for an existing Support connection and case collection. Its original release initialization and immutable configuration publication resume in the same selected output.

## Continue customer work

Receive the whole case package through **Complete delivery**, then open the receiving case named by the original completion. Keep that case directory and native source directory together through reopening. The package retains the complete captured sender history and every original native source archive.

# Product source selections

The original distribution builder can package a complete product from the same
Git commit as the full toolkit. A committed recipe chooses base registrations,
whole source-owned contributions, component directories and explicit support
files. The existing Git reader, source manifest, runtime profile, installer,
Applications launcher and recovery commands remain the distribution workflow.

## Complete runtime and browser source

A selected component carries the maintained browser route maps for its included
HTTP servers. The builder uses the same JSON manifests as those servers, so a
browser import such as `./operations.mjs` resolves through its served URL to
the original shared module. Console, job intake and job resolution maps are
included when their original server components are selected. Every map and
mapped file appears in the package's ordinary source manifest.

Static Node imports continue to use normalized repository paths. If an
imported production helper has an acceptance-like filename, its explicit
declaration in the original base support inventory permits that exact file.
The builder adds it only when a selected module imports it. Original file and
directory exclusions still apply to imported modules and browser assets.

These source dependencies leave the recipe's command, package-export, provider
and runtime-feature choices intact. Explicitly selecting an excluded browser
server remains an invalid package and reports the missing packaged entry.

## Build through the runtime workspace

The private runtime workspace's **Build a product** view discovers the recipes
at the chosen commit, reviews the complete selected product, builds its original
package, and opens the resulting archive in **Source & profile**. It retains the
same request and output through interruption and provides the original package
download. Follow [the complete browser and CLI workflow](runtime-workspace/SOURCE_BUILDS.md)
for source selection, adapter installation and recovery.

## Build a product

Run the maintained builder from a repository that contains the selected commit:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/checkout --ref ORIGINAL_COMMIT \
  --selection water-operations --out /absolute/water-release

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/checkout --ref ORIGINAL_COMMIT \
  --selection woo-merchant --out /absolute/woo-release

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/checkout --ref ORIGINAL_COMMIT \
  --selection grant-reviewer --out /absolute/grant-reviewer-release
```

Use any selection ID from the table below in the same build command and give
that product its own output directory.

Replace `ORIGINAL_COMMIT` with the full original commit SHA. Each output directory
belongs to one source commit and selection. The packaged receipt names the
archive, SHA-256, installed/source bytes, source acquisition and materialization.
The manifest adds `sourceSelection`: original recipe ID, title, path, Git blob,
SHA-256 and byte length. Its recipe also appears in the normal file inventory
and `distributionInputs`.

The package version includes both the commit and selection, for example
`0.1.0-source.g0123456789ab.selection.water-operations`. The full package retains
the original `0.1.0-source.g0123456789ab` version form.

# Invoice payment requests on Stellar

This collection workflow starts with an issued customer invoice, produces a reviewed Stellar wallet request, and brings the returned transaction into the same customer receipts and invoice allocations used by merchant accounting. The browser, command line, HTTP client, and native workspace share the original accounting directory and operation journal.

Open the merchant receivables workspace and select an issued invoice with an amount due. Choose **Payment requests** to review the selected invoice amount, the exact Stellar destination and asset, the wallet amount, memo, and expiry. The issued request retains the original invoice document identity and its balance at review.

## Collection terms

Each request has two explicit amounts:

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `invoiceAmount` | The amount of the invoice currency this collection will settle. It defaults to the current amount due. |
| `stellarAmount` | The exact amount the merchant must receive on Stellar, expressed as a decimal string with up to seven decimal places. |
| `valuationNote` | The merchant's recorded basis for applying that Stellar payment to the selected invoice amount. |

The original invoice remains in its own currency. For example, a USD invoice may select an agreed amount of a specifically issued Stellar asset. Enter its exact asset code and issuer and record the agreed valuation. Native XLM at the exact face amount of an XLM invoice supplies its own face-value description.

The destination is the merchant's existing Stellar G account. The asset is either `{kind:"native"}` or `{kind:"credit",code,issuer}`. Issued assets with the same code and different issuers are distinct assets.

The default memo is a unique `MEMO_HASH` bound to this request and the original invoice. Keep that memo in the wallet transaction. A supplied memo supports `MEMO_TEXT`, `MEMO_ID`, `MEMO_HASH`, or `MEMO_RETURN`; hash and return memo values are canonical base64 of 32 bytes. The wallet message, `msg`, is separate from the transaction memo.

The wallet handoff follows the original [Stellar SEP-7 payment URI standard](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/master/ecosystem/sep-0007.md). It uses an unsigned `web+stellar:pay` URI containing the exact destination, amount, asset and memo. The customer opens that URI in their selected wallet and reviews the transaction there. The selected Stellar test network is carried explicitly in the URI's network passphrase.

## Review and issue a request

A preview returns the complete canonical `proposal`, its `reviewSha256`, the current invoice summary, and the workspace `revision`. Issuing uses those exact returned proposal bytes and review digest together with the operator and a stable operation identifier.

The native controller rereads the original issued invoice before issuing. A changed invoice balance, version, or collection term requires a current review. Outstanding active requests on the same invoice and network reserve their selected invoice amounts; their sum must fit the amount due. Withdraw a replaced request before issuing a replacement for its reserved amount.

Example collection terms for an issued USD 125 invoice:

```json
{
  "invoiceAmount": "125.00",
  "network": "stellar:pubnet",
  "destination": "YOUR_EXISTING_MERCHANT_G_ACCOUNT",
  "asset": {
    "kind": "credit",
    "code": "USD",
    "issuer": "THE_EXACT_AGREED_ASSET_ISSUER_G_ACCOUNT"
  },
  "stellarAmount": "125.0000000",
  "msg": "Payment for the issued invoice",
  "valuationNote": "USD 125.00 of this invoice is settled by receipt of 125.0000000 units of the selected issued asset."
}
```

Replace the account placeholders with the actual existing destination and agreed issuer. For native XLM, use `{"kind":"native"}`. An optional expiry is a future UTC timestamp, such as an operator-selected date ending in `Z`.

### Command line

The installed `starforge` command uses the existing receivables entrypoint. Reopen the original accounting directory.

```sh
starforge receivables payment-preview --directory /private/accounting --invoice INVOICE_UUID --input /private/payment-terms.json --out /private/payment-review.json
```

The review file is created exclusively: an existing file is preserved. Inspect the returned proposal and wallet URI. Build the issue input from that same review:

```js
import {readFile, writeFile} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {randomUUID} from 'node:crypto';

const reviewed = JSON.parse(await readFile('/private/payment-review.json', 'utf8'));
const issue = {
  revision: reviewed.revision,
  actor: 'Merchant accounts',
  requestId: randomUUID(),
  proposal: reviewed.proposal,
  reviewSha256: reviewed.reviewSha256,
};
await writeFile('/private/payment-issue.json', JSON.stringify(issue, null, 2) + '\n',
  {flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600});
```

Issue the reviewed request:

```sh
starforge receivables payment-create --directory /private/accounting --invoice INVOICE_UUID --input /private/payment-issue.json
```

The result includes `paymentRequest.id`, the updated invoice, workspace revision and original operation. Retain the input for recovery. Download the customer handoff using the returned request ID:

```sh
starforge receivables payment-file --directory /private/accounting --id PAYMENT_REQUEST_UUID --name payment-request.html --out /private/customer-payment-request.html
starforge receivables payment-file --directory /private/accounting --id PAYMENT_REQUEST_UUID --name payment-request.uri --out /private/customer-payment-request.uri
```

The HTML shows the invoice, selected invoice amount, exact wallet terms and current request status. Its wallet button is available when the request remains payable. The URI file contains the original wallet handoff with one terminating newline.

## Receive the returned wallet transaction

Record the original 64-character lowercase transaction hash supplied by the wallet. The sender's Stellar G account is an optional exact constraint. When it is omitted, the verifier derives the paying account from the matching original operation; this also handles a separate transaction fee payer.

The return record captures the reference and operator note. Receiving then reads the original Stellar network and transaction response through the configured native verifier. The transfer must match the saved network, merchant destination, asset, received amount and transaction memo. The original ledger result and operation identify the transfer.

For a public-network transfer, successful receiving creates an ordinary customer receipt with its original ledger close date, recorded invoice valuation and complete source references. The default allocation applies as much of that invoice-valued receipt as fits the invoice's current and retained dated balances. Any remaining receipt amount stays available in the existing customer account.

The receipt and allocation are committed with the verification observation in the same accounting operation. The same transaction cannot become a second receipt through another request or another import. Reopening a received reference returns its original receipt and allocation.

### Return input

Read the current workspace revision with `starforge receivables state` and put it in the input together with a newly generated request ID:

```json
{
  "revision": 42,
  "actor": "Merchant accounts",
  "requestId": "A_NEW_OPERATION_UUID",
  "transaction": "THE_EXACT_64_CHARACTER_LOWERCASE_TRANSACTION_HASH",
  "note": "Wallet transaction returned for this invoice."
}
```

Use the actual revision and generated UUID from this workspace, then record the reference:

```sh
starforge receivables payment-return --directory /private/accounting --id PAYMENT_REQUEST_UUID --input /private/payment-return.json
```

The result supplies `paymentReturn.id`. Use it with the returned current revision in the receiving operation:

```json
{
  "revision": 43,
  "actor": "Merchant accounts",
  "requestId": "ANOTHER_NEW_OPERATION_UUID",
  "returnId": "PAYMENT_RETURN_UUID",
  "allocate": true
}
```

```sh
starforge receivables payment-receive --directory /private/accounting --id PAYMENT_REQUEST_UUID --input /private/payment-receive.json
```

Optional `allocatedDate` chooses the accounting allocation date. It must be on or after the invoice issue date and original ledger close date. Optional `allocationAmount` chooses an exact amount that fits the received value and the retained invoice balances. Set `allocate:false` to record the verified customer receipt for later allocation; omit `allocationAmount` in that case.

The merchant's selected `invoiceAmount` determines the invoice-currency receipt value. The complete original asset, atomic amount, destination, payer, memo, network, ledger, transaction fingerprint and valuation note remain attached to its source.

### Correct a reported transaction or sending account

In the operator workspace, open the invoice's payment request and its transaction receiving history.

- **Transaction reported against the wrong invoice:** keep that report in its original history. Open the correct invoice's issued request and record the same transaction hash there. An unverified or unsuccessful report does not reserve the payment. Receiving checks the selected request's exact wallet terms.
- **Transaction reported as a refund by mistake:** open the correct invoice's issued request, record the original hash and receive it there. An unverified or unsuccessful refund report remains in its history and does not reserve the payment. A refund whose outgoing transfer was verified keeps ownership while its funding or accounting record is reconciled; use [the original refund return](./REFUNDS_AND_CREDITS.md#reconcile-an-outgoing-transfer-that-already-happened) for that recovery.
- **Incorrect transaction hash:** record the correct hash as another transaction reference. Each reference keeps its original hash, operator note and observations.
- **Incorrect optional sending account:** choose **Correct sending account** on the saved reference, enter the correct G account or leave it blank to use the payment's actual sender, and provide the reason. Then choose **Inspect and receive** again.

The sending account can be corrected before the reference has a verified transfer. Its returned-reference ID, original hash, original report note and previous observations remain in place. The request history records the previous account, new account, operator, correction time and reason. A successful public-network receipt or test-network verification keeps the verified account fixed.

The same correction is available through the existing `payment-return` command and `reportPaymentReturn` client method. Reuse the saved payment-request ID and transaction hash, with the current revision and a new operation ID. Include an explicit account string to change the sender constraint, or `"payer": null` to clear it:

```json
{
  "revision": 44,
  "actor": "Merchant accounts",
  "requestId": "A_NEW_CORRECTION_OPERATION_UUID",
  "transaction": "THE_ORIGINAL_SAVED_64_CHARACTER_TRANSACTION_HASH",
  "payer": null,
  "note": "Use the account that sent the payment; the earlier optional account was entered incorrectly."
}
```

Omitting `payer` preserves the saved account constraint. Replaying an uncertain correction uses the same operation ID and unchanged input. A further correction uses a new operation ID and current revision.

Verified receiving owns the transfer. A transaction already recorded as a receipt, including a later reversed receipt, cannot create another receipt. Accepted test-network receiving also remains unique. The receiver compares both inner and outer transaction hashes for fee-bump transactions, so changing the reported form of the same transaction does not duplicate it. Open the existing receiving result to reconcile an already verified payment.

### Test network and incomplete observations

The same reviewed request and original-network verification are available on `stellar:testnet`. A matching test-network transfer produces `TESTNET_VERIFIED` and retains its original observation and proof. The commercial receipt and allocation path applies to verified public-network transfers.

The receiving result keeps the actual observation:

| Observation | Operator action |
| --- | --- |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Keep the original return and receive it again after the transaction becomes available. |
| `VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE` | Reopen the original return, resolve the reported transport or response problem, and perform another receiving observation. |
| `FAILED` | Inspect the original failed ledger result. The still-current request can present its wallet handoff for a new transaction. |
| `TRANSFER_PRECEDES_REQUEST` | Inspect the supplied transaction against the request's original issue time. |
| `TRANSFER_AFTER_EXPIRY` or `TRANSFER_AFTER_CANCELLATION` | Use the retained ledger close time and request history to resolve the late transfer. |
| `TESTNET_VERIFIED` | Open the retained test-network proof for the demonstration or integration record. |

Each new receiving observation uses a new operation ID. Recovery of an uncertain existing operation reuses its original operation ID and unchanged input.

## Reopen, withdraw and reconcile

List requests for an invoice or customer:

```sh
starforge receivables payment-requests --directory /private/accounting --invoice INVOICE_UUID --offset 0 --limit 100
starforge receivables payment-requests --directory /private/accounting --customer CUSTOMER_UUID --as-of 2026-10-12
```

The page returns its total, offset, limit and workspace revision. Use the next offset to continue the same query. The maximum page size is 500.

Open an existing request with all returned references, receipt links, allocations and history:

```sh
starforge receivables payment-request --directory /private/accounting --id PAYMENT_REQUEST_UUID
```

The summary shows selected invoice value, current amount due, received, applied and unapplied amounts. `balanceChanged` identifies a balance change since the reviewed invoice snapshot. Request status is calculated from the original receipt and allocation records. Releasing an allocation or voiding a receipt through the normal receivables commands is reflected when the request is reopened.

Dated `asOf` views use the selected accounting date for balances. Expiry and payable status use the response's explicit `observedAt` timestamp. Keep those two times with an exported report.

To withdraw a request, use `payment-cancel` with the current mutation context and a clear reason:

```json
{
  "revision": 44,
  "actor": "Merchant accounts",
  "requestId": "A_NEW_WITHDRAWAL_OPERATION_UUID",
  "reason": "Replaced with the customer's reviewed asset and collection terms."
}
```

```sh
starforge receivables payment-cancel --directory /private/accounting --id PAYMENT_REQUEST_UUID --input /private/payment-withdrawal.json
```

Withdrawal records its time and reason, preserves the issued request and returns, and releases that request's active reservation. Reopen the same ID to inspect it later. Issue any replacement from a new current preview. Existing receipts and allocations retain their ordinary accounting history.

## TypeScript and JavaScript client

The default distribution package is `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant`. If the installed package's `package.json` declares a different name, use that name with the same export suffix:

```ts
import {
  createReceivablesClient,
  type PaymentRequestInput,
  type PaymentRequestDetail,
} from '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/receivables/client';

const client = createReceivablesClient({
  baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:8448/api/receivables',
});

const terms: PaymentRequestInput = {
  network: 'stellar:pubnet',
  destination: merchantReceivingAccount,
  asset: {kind: 'native'},
  stellarAmount: agreedStellarAmount,
  invoiceAmount: agreedInvoiceAmount,
  valuationNote: agreedValuation,
};

const review = await client.previewPaymentRequest(invoiceId, terms);
// Present review.proposal to the operator and retain this exact review.
const created = await client.createPaymentRequest(invoiceId, {
  revision: review.revision,
  actor: 'Merchant accounts',
  requestId: crypto.randomUUID(),
  proposal: review.proposal,
  reviewSha256: review.reviewSha256,
});

const returned = await client.reportPaymentReturn(created.paymentRequest.id, {
  revision: created.revision,
  actor: 'Merchant accounts',
  requestId: crypto.randomUUID(),
  transaction: walletTransactionHash,
});

const received = await client.receivePaymentRequest(created.paymentRequest.id, {
  revision: returned.revision,
  actor: 'Merchant accounts',
  requestId: crypto.randomUUID(),
  returnId: returned.paymentReturn.id,
  allocate: true,
});

const detail: PaymentRequestDetail = await client.paymentRequest(created.paymentRequest.id);
const printable = await client.paymentRequestBytes(created.paymentRequest.id, 'payment-request.html');
const receiving = await client.paymentRequestBytes(created.paymentRequest.id, 'receiving.json');
```

The example uses variables supplied by the actual invoice, merchant configuration and wallet result. Amounts stay decimal strings throughout.

All new client methods accept an optional `{signal}` in the final argument. `paymentRequestFile` returns the original HTTP `Response`; `paymentRequestBytes` reads it into a `Uint8Array` and returns its name and media type. The client preserves the server's error code, details, request identifier and response.

The browser uses the default same-origin API base. A Node caller supplies the full local API URL and, if required by its environment, a fetch implementation. The client sends each mutation once. A transport interruption retains the same mutation input for reconciliation and retry; constructing a new operation would create a different request.

### Methods and routes

| Client method | HTTP route |
| --- | --- |
| `previewPaymentRequest(invoiceId, terms)` | `POST /invoices/:invoiceId/payment-requests/preview` |
| `createPaymentRequest(invoiceId, input)` | `POST /invoices/:invoiceId/payment-requests` |
| `paymentRequests(query)` | `GET /payment-requests` |
| `paymentRequest(id, query)` | `GET /payment-requests/:id` |
| `cancelPaymentRequest(id, input)` | `POST /payment-requests/:id/cancel` |
| `reportPaymentReturn(id, input)` | `POST /payment-requests/:id/returns` |
| `receivePaymentRequest(id, input)` | `POST /payment-requests/:id/receive` |
| `paymentRequestFile(id, name)` | `GET /payment-requests/:id/files/:name` |

Routes are relative to `/api/receivables`. Preview is a read-only calculation submitted as JSON. The mutation routes use `actor`, stable `requestId` and current `revision`; create additionally requires the original reviewed proposal and digest.

Existing automation using `receivables apply` can select `payment-create`, `payment-cancel`, `payment-return`, or `payment-receive`. Its `--id` is the invoice ID for `payment-create` and the payment-request ID for the other three actions.

## Original files and workspace recovery

| File selector | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `payment-request.json` | Exact immutable issued request, original proposal and review digest. |
| `payment-request.html` | Printable customer request with current summary and wallet handoff. |
| `payment-request.uri` | Original SEP-7 URI. |
| `status.json` | Current summary, request history and accounting revision. |
| `receiving.json` | Original request, request history, returns, complete original proofs, receipts and allocations. |
| `proof-RETURN_UUID.json` | One returned transaction with its complete native observations and resulting receipt and allocations. |

The request record holds compact proof references. Complete original verification responses are retained under the original accounting workspace's `exports` directory as `transfer-proof.json`, with byte length and SHA-256. The receiving and proof downloads verify and hydrate those originals.

Keep the original accounting workspace, including its existing `exports` files, when moving or backing up the workspace. Download the customer account through the existing `receivables export` command and retain the corresponding request and receiving files for the collection handoff.

Reopening the same workspace restores the request register and original operation journal. If a mutation response is lost, first reopen the invoice or request and retain the unchanged input. Reusing its stable operation ID recovers the original operation instead of duplicating its issued request or received payment. A definitive revision or review conflict calls for a current view and a newly reviewed operation.

## Native integration

The maintained distribution exposes:

| Export | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/receivables/client` | Typed HTTP client for browser and local integrations. |
| `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/receivables/payment-requests` | Original proposal, URI, document and summary model. |
| `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/receivables/payment-requests-workspace` | Payment request controller over an existing receivables workspace. |
| `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/receivables/payment-requests-verifier` | Native Stellar SDK and original-network transfer verification. |

The normal `ReceivablesWorkspace` supplies these operations through its facade, so embedded callers use the same receipt, allocation and history behavior as the HTTP server. The lower-level workspace accepts a `verifyTransfer` implementation for an existing native host; its result must preserve the original network and transaction observations required by the model.

The selected source distribution includes the native network catalog and maintained SDK package anchor. Runtime installation uses the existing Stellar SDK 16.3.0 dependency profile and the original [Stellar RPC transaction interface](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/apis/rpc/api-reference/methods/getTransaction).
